title: Republicans have ‘nothing to run on’ in midterms after Trump failures, Jeffries says
summary: House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries says Republicans have "nothing to run on" in the November midterms after President Trump broke promises to lower costs and avoid new wars. Jeffries cited a New Jersey voter-registration software error, rising prices and a US-Israel conflict with Iran that has caused casualties and higher living costs. He said Democrats will campaign on affordability while Republicans seek a case for a GOP-controlled Congress.
content:
Top House Democrat says US president ‘failed to deliver’ on campaign promises to lower costs and avoid overseas wars

Donald Trump’s Republican party has “nothing to run on” for the congressionalmidterm electionsafter the president broke promises to lower costs and avoid starting war overseas, the US House minority leader,Hakeem Jeffries, has said.

The New York congressman made those comments on CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday, exactly 100 days from the 3 November midterms, when Jeffries and his fellowDemocratsare aiming to take control of the US House and Senate from their Republican opponents.

Asked to discuss the elections, Jeffries alluded to how Trump and other Republicans quicklyseized ona 21 July announcement from the Democratic New Jersey governor, Mikie Sherrill, that 6,600 noncitizens in the state had registered to vote because of a software error.

Fewer than 400 of them voted before the identification and correction of the error. But the president and his allies nonetheless used the disclosure toboostfalse claimsthat there are scores of noncitizens on voter rolls who could compromise the integrity of the midterms, during which Republicans are predicted to lose seats.

Jeffries on Sunday argued that was because it is a more comfortable strategy to adopt rather than confront how the US and Israeli militaries beganwarringwith Iran in February after Trump won a second presidency in 2024 havingpromised“not to start … endless wars in the Middle East”.

The costs of the war have included thedeathsof 18 US service members as of Sunday, along with injuries to hundreds more. Gas and grocery prices have alsosoaredamid the conflict, leaving 95% of Americans believing that the US is suffering an affordability crisis, according to exclusivepollingconducted for the Guardian.

Karoline Leavitt, the White House press secretary, on Sunday acknowledged there was an affordability crisis in the US – but argued the blame for that fell onDemocratsand Joe Biden’s presidency.

"All these things will only get better if given two more years with a Republican Congress" in November, Leavittsaidon Fox News.

Speaking to State of the Union host Dana Bash, Jeffriessaid, "Republicans … have failed to actually deliver on making life more affordable for the American people."

He continued, "It wasDonald Trumpwho promised to lower costs on day one. But we know that costs haven’t gone down in this country. Costs have gone up.

"It was Donald Trump … who said that he was elected not to start wars, endless wars in the Middle East, but to stop them – and then turned around and has gotten us involved in this reckless war of choice in Iran that has skyrocketed gaspriceson the American people."

Jeffries then referred to how Republicans a year earliercutmore than $1tn from Medicaid, the public health insurance program for people in the US who are low-income and disabled, adding: "They have nothing to run on. We’re going to run on fighting for an affordable America.

"Too many people are working hard – they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive," Jeffries alsosaid. "And they can barely survive, not enough food on the table, not enough gas in the tank, unable to actually regularly and consistently afford to pay the rent or pay the mortgage."

A recent analysis fromDecision Desk HQforecasts that Democrats are likely to win amajorityin the House – and that Republicans are narrowly favored to retain control of the US Senate.

markdown_content:
## Top House Democrat says US president ‘failed to deliver’ on campaign promises to lower costs and avoid overseas wars

Donald Trump’s Republican party has “nothing to run on” for the congressional midterm elections after the president broke promises to lower costs and avoid starting war overseas, the US House minority leader, Hakeem Jeffries, has said.

The New York congressman made those comments on CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday, exactly 100 days from the 3 November midterms, when Jeffries and his fellow Democrats are aiming to take control of the US House and Senate from their Republican opponents.

## Incident Details

Asked to discuss the elections, Jeffries alluded to how Trump and other Republicans quickly seized on a 21 July announcement from the Democratic New Jersey governor, Mikie Sherrill, that 6,600 noncitizens in the state had registered to vote because of a software error.

Fewer than 400 of them voted before the identification and correction of the error. But the president and his allies nonetheless used the disclosure to boost false claims that there are scores of noncitizens on voter rolls who could compromise the integrity of the midterms, during which Republicans are predicted to lose seats.

Jeffries on Sunday argued that was because it is a more comfortable strategy to adopt rather than confront how the US and Israeli militaries began warring with Iran in February after Trump won a second presidency in 2024 having promised “not to start … endless wars in the Middle East”.

## Costs and impact

The costs of the war have included the deaths of 18 US service members as of Sunday, along with injuries to hundreds more. Gas and grocery prices have also soared amid the conflict, leaving 95% of Americans believing that the US is suffering an affordability crisis, according to exclusive polling conducted for the Guardian.

Key details:
- 18 US service members killed (as of Sunday)
- Hundreds more injured
- 95% of Americans believe the US is facing an affordability crisis (Guardian polling)

## White House response

Karoline Leavitt, the White House press secretary, on Sunday acknowledged there was an affordability crisis in the US – but argued the blame for that fell on Democrats and Joe Biden’s presidency.

> “All these things will only get better if given two more years with a Republican Congress,” Leavitt said on Fox News.

## Jeffries’s remarks

Speaking to State of the Union host Dana Bash, Jeffries said:

> “Republicans … have failed to actually deliver on making life more affordable for the American people.”

He continued:

> “It was Donald Trump who promised to lower costs on day one. But we know that costs haven’t gone down in this country. Costs have gone up.
>
> “It was Donald Trump … who said that he was elected not to start wars, endless wars in the Middle East, but to stop them – and then turned around and has gotten us involved in this reckless war of choice in Iran that has skyrocketed gas prices on the American people.”

Jeffries then referred to how Republicans a year earlier cut more than $1tn from Medicaid, the public health insurance program for people in the US who are low-income and disabled, adding:

> “They have nothing to run on. We’re going to run on fighting for an affordable America.
>
> “Too many people are working hard – they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive. And they can barely survive, not enough food on the table, not enough gas in the tank, unable to actually regularly and consistently afford to pay the rent or pay the mortgage.”

## Political context and outlook

A recent analysis from Decision Desk HQ forecasts that Democrats are likely to win a majority in the House – and that Republicans are narrowly favored to retain control of the US Senate.
